title: Associate Director, Agentic Computational Platform
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
As Associate Director/Director of Agentic Computational Platform within the Physical Sciences AI division, you will lead and grow the team responsible for the software infrastructure that enables Lila's scientific superintelligence to autonomously construct, execute, and interpret complex physics-based simulations. Beyond your direct team, you will serve as a senior engineering leader across a broader portfolio of cross-disciplinary scientific computing efforts — coordinating strategy across workstreams that extend beyond your reporting structure and partnering closely with research and product leadership to bring Lila's scientific intelligence to customers at scale. This role requires both strong people leadership and the technical credibility to drive alignment and execution across a multi-team engineering portfolio.
What You'll Be Building
- Lead, hire, and develop a high-performing team of engineers and scientists; set the bar for technical excellence and foster a culture of collaboration and rapid iteration.
- Drive engineering strategy and coordination across a portfolio of cross-disciplinary scientific computing workstreams, including teams outside your direct organization; ensure coherent technical direction, shared standards, and well-sequenced delivery across the broader program.
- Define and own the technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap for your team's core platform capabilities, setting architectural direction for agentic frameworks, integration layers, and heterogeneous compute platforms — in close alignment with Physical Sciences AI research priorities and company goals.
- Build deep partnerships with AI research, platform, infrastructure, and software teams to translate scientific requirements into production-grade capabilities; serve as a primary point of engineering accountability for cross-team delivery and impact.
- Own execution across your direct team: prioritize projects, manage trade-offs, remove blockers, and ensure the team ships with high quality and velocity.
- Represent the broader engineering program to senior leadership and external collaborators; communicate technical strategy, cross-team progress, and business impact clearly.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- MS/PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, ML/AI, Scientific Computing, or a related technical field.
- Proven experience leading and growing engineering or research teams, including hiring, performance management, and career development.
- Track record of setting technical vision and delivering complex, multi-year platform or infrastructure initiatives in a fast-moving environment.
- Strong technical depth in ML-driven pipelines, agentic frameworks, or scientific workflow systems — enough to earn trust across teams, drive sound architectural decisions, and influence engineering direction across a multi-workstream program without direct authority over every contributor.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to operate effectively across research, engineering, and executive audiences.
Bonus Points For
- Experience leading teams building agentic frameworks, autonomous ML pipelines, or multi-step tool-using agents — particularly for scientific or computational applications — and scaling those teams from early-stage to mature, high-output organizations.
- Background in physics-based simulation infrastructure, large-scale scientific workflow orchestration, or automated computational experiment platforms; familiarity with the software and computational patterns that underpin atomistic, electronic structure, or surrogate-driven modeling workflows.
- Experience navigating the intersection of deep research and production engineering — knowing when to invest in infrastructure versus move fast.
- Familiarity with data-centric engineering practices: streaming systems, provenance tracking, distributed metadata services, or large-scale data orchestration.
- Sufficient depth in advanced ML techniques relevant to agentic reasoning (e.g., planning models, tool-using agents, RLHF/RLAIF workflows) to evaluate technical approaches and guide research-engineering tradeoffs.
- Familiarity with materials science simulation codes (VASP, LAMMPS) or workflow frameworks (atomate, aiida) is a plus.
Compensation
We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.
U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.
International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.
Expected Base Salary Range
$288,000 — $480,000 USD

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.
LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. title: Associate Director / Director, Customer Program Management, Physical Sciences
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences is building a new Customer Delivery & Success function, and we're looking for an Associate Director / Director, Customer Program Management to lead delivery for our physical sciences customer partnerships. In this role, you're bringing LILA's science into the real world with customers. This is a senior, hands-on role that sits at the center of high-value, multi-year customer engagements: you will be the primary face of LILA to the customer, the operational owner of a complex program spanning multiple concurrent projects, and a founding contributor to how LILA delivers for customers as we scale.
This is not a lightweight, account management role. Our engagements are deeply technical and highly consultative, and the customer relies on you to understand where the science is, where the program is headed, and what it will take to get there. You'll coordinate across a wide set of internal teams (e.g., AI/ML researchers, experimentalists, automation and hardware engineers, software, product) while owning the customer relationship end to end and shaping where it grows next.
The role has three core dimensions:
- Customer engagement and growth: serving as the primary conduit to the customer, managing the relationship holistically, and recognizing and shaping opportunities to mature the engagement.
- Program management: driving cross-functional operational excellence in a complex scientific environment so that delivery happens to scope, on time, and with quality.
- Delivery infrastructure: helping stand up a new function by building the processes, tooling, and operating models that define what customer delivery looks like across LILA.
What You'll Be Building
Customer Engagement & Growth
- Intentional Relationship Management : Serve as the primary contact and trusted operational interface for the customer, owning the health and trajectory of the relationship over time.
- Clear & Structured Communication : Translate complex internal program status into clear, structured communication for the customer– surfacing and steering milestones, risks, and decisions.
- Trust-Building Governance : steering committees, milestone reviews, deliverable handoffs, and the difficult conversations (delays, quality incidents, scope changes) that sustain trust through the hard moments.
- Customer Renewal & Expansion : Identify and shape opportunities to grow the engagement, partnering with business development and product to bring them to life.
Program Management
- Operational Excellence: Own end-to-end delivery across multiple concurrent projects under a single partnership timelines, resourcing, milestone tracking, dependency & risk management. Promote a high-performance team environment through operational rigor across the program, coaching the wider team toward practices that outlast any one person.
- Cross-Functional Alignment: Coordinate a cross-functional "team of teams" that speaks different technical languages, keeping everyone aligned on shared objectives and clear on priorities and decision points.
- Shared Truth & Situational Awareness : Structure and run effective program meetings, decision forums, and reporting so the right information reaches the right people at the right time.
- Strategic Judgment: Hold many considerations at once (e.g., customer needs, technical constraints, resourcing, risk) and exercise the judgment to chart a course when there's no obviously right answer, recommending a path forward and knowing when to rethink the approach entirely rather than optimize the current one.
Delivery Infrastructure
- Building for Scale: Help build the operating model for customer delivery at Lila: scalable processes, templates, tooling, and best practices that extend well beyond this single program.
- Setting the Standard : Define what operational excellence and delivery success look like for the function, including the metrics and KPIs worth tracking.
- Servant Leadership: Lead with Lila's broader mission in view and contribute to a founding team of delivery leaders be generous with hard-won lessons, invest in your peers' success, and build the low-visibility shared infrastructure that lifts the whole function rather than only your own program.
What You'll Need to Succeed

- Sound judgment about customer relationship health over time: knowing when to push, when to absorb, when to escalate, and how to deliver hard news in a way that strengthens rather than erodes trust.

title: Associate Director/Director, Frontier and AI Product Counsel
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
As Associate Director/Director, Frontier and AI Product Counsel at Lila Sciences, you will be the dedicated legal partner to the teams building Scientific Superintelligence™ — our AI research organization, our AI Science Factory™ platform, and the data, safety, and security functions that support them. You will own the legal questions that come with training frontier models on scientific data and running experiments autonomously: where data comes from and what we can do with it, how rights are allocated when we discover something alongside a partner, what we can publish or open-source, and how we build, evaluate, and release capable systems responsibly.
This is deliberately a build role, not a maintenance role. Much of this work has no settled precedent and no off-the-shelf playbook — you will frequently be designing the framework rather than applying one. You'll partner daily with scientists, ML researchers, platform engineers, and our safety and security teams, and closely with our privacy, commercial, and go-to-market colleagues as the platform is deployed, and you'll be the person who translates between technical reality and legal risk in both directions.
This role reports to the Vice President, Associate General Counsel, Product and is scoped for an experienced attorney with 7–12 years of experience who wants to work at the intersection of law, AI, and science, and who is energized rather than unsettled by novel questions. You should be comfortable with ambiguity, opinionated about risk, and willing to sit with a research team long enough to actually understand what they're building.
What You'll Be Building
Data and model development
- Advise research and data teams on permissible data usage across the training pipeline, and build the provenance and acquisition frameworks that govern what goes into Lila's models
- Serve as a subject matter expert on copyright, licensing, privacy, and contractual restrictions as applied to training data — public, licensed, synthetic, open-source, and partner-contributed alike
- Support structuring and negotiation of data licensing, material transfer, consortium, and research collaboration agreements with academic, clinical, and industry partners, including how rights in data, models, and derived outputs are allocated
Release and disclosure
- Advise on release decisions for models, agents, tools, and datasets, including open-weight strategy and the application of open-source licenses to incoming and outgoing code, data, and model artifacts
- Coordinate legal readiness for model and platform launches — model documentation and system cards, capability evaluations, and review of pre-release and internal-only models
- Support publication and disclosure review, balancing scientific openness against partner obligations and safety considerations
- Counsel research teams on research design, data collection and sharing, external collaborations, and program launches, including alignment, interpretability, and societal-impact work as those functions develop
- Counsel platform teams on legal considerations for autonomous experimentation and agentic systems
Safety, security, and dual-use
- Partner with our AI Safety and AI Security teams on the legal dimensions of technical mitigations, evaluations, red-teaming, and misuse prevention, including vendor engagements and external collaborations
- Advise on dual-use and biosecurity considerations arising from autonomous chemistry and biology, including screening, access controls, and disclosure
- Help operationalize Lila's safety framework as capabilities scale: how capability thresholds translate into evaluations, access controls, documented mitigations, and release decisions
- Serve as a first-line contact for safety and security escalations, and build the playbooks that let that response scale
Regulation and infrastructure
- Track and translate the regulatory landscape that bears on our work: emerging AI regimes (EU AI Act, US state AI laws), health and research data rules, human-subject and biospecimen requirements, and export controls
- Support compute and infrastructure arrangements, including cloud and datacenter agreements, cross-border data transfers, and data localization
- Represent Lila in regulatory inquiries, and contribute to industry and academic work on data governance and safety norms for AI-driven science
Building the function
- Design the frameworks, templates, and self-serve guidance that put legal judgment in the hands of the teams who need it, and use AI tools aggressively to extend the reach of a small team
What You'll Need to Succeed
- J.D. and membership in at least one U.S. state bar in good standing
- 7–12 years of legal experience, with substantial time in-house at a technology, AI, or life sciences company, ideally spanning both research-facing and product- or customer-facing counseling
- Depth in at least two of: copyright and IP, data licensing and provenance, privacy and data protection, AI regulation, model launch and deployment counseling, or research and collaboration transactions — and the appetite to get up to speed fast on the rest
- Genuine technical fluency: you can hold your own in a conversation about how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed, you can read a research protocol without needing it translated, and you can spot the legal issue inside a technical design
- Sound judgment under uncertainty, and the ability to give clear, practical advice on questions where the law has not caught up, including when to be flexible and when to hold a line
- A strong sense of ownership and the instinct to build cross-functional relationships, so teams bring you in while decisions are still open rather than after them
- Excellent written communication — you can draft a policy, a framework, or a whitepaper that non-lawyers will actually use
- Comfort operating outside your areas of expertise, wearing many hats, and moving at startup speed without losing rigor
Bonus Points For
- A STEM background or advanced degree, particularly in biology, chemistry, materials, or computer science
- Experience advising AI research teams on training data, model development, or model release decisions
- Experience advising on enterprise or API product deployment — data governance, tenancy and access controls, connectors, or agentic features
- Experience coordinating model launches, or drafting model documentation, system cards, or capability evaluation write-ups
- Experience with AI-generated invention and inventorship questions, or patent strategy in an AI-driven discovery setting
- Familiarity with dual-use, biosecurity, export control, or CFIUS considerations
- Experience supporting academic collaborations, consortium agreements, or federally funded research
- An academic or publishing background, or depth in open-source and data licensing
- Experience engaging directly with regulators or standards bodies
- Experience building legal infrastructure and scalable processes from scratch
- Enthusiasm for transforming legal practice through AI and data-driven tools

title: Associate Director/Director, Inference Engineering
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is hiring an Associate Director/Director, Inference Engineering to lead the team responsible for Lila's model serving platform: the inference APIs, serving frameworks, request routing, batching strategies, and deployment systems that bring models reliably to production.
You will define how Lila serves models at scale, balancing latency, throughput, quality, and cost, and act as the technical authority connecting research and ML to production-grade serving capabilities. The work spans people leadership, service ownership, cross-functional partnership, and deep technical judgment in modern LLM serving.
What You'll Be Building
- Own the inference service end to end: API contracts, latency SLAs, throughput guarantees, rate limits
- Drive serving architecture decisions: batching, KV cache, speculative decoding, quantization, multi-node deployment
- Establish SLOs for latency, throughput, and availability, plus on-call and postmortem practices
- Partner with ML, research, and product engineering to make new models production-ready
- Build systems for model onboarding, deployment safety, evaluation gates, and observability
- Build, mentor, and retain a high-performing engineering team, and own the serving roadmap

title: Co-Op, Bayesian Methods for Complex Decision Making
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences builds AI systems that accelerate discovery across the physical and life sciences. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next.
Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search.
As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns.
What You'll Be Building
- Design and benchmark experiment-selection strategies that balance exploration and exploitation under realistic budgets
- Build autonomous discovery agents that propose the next experiment from surrogate models
- Develop in-context learning approaches inspired by Bayesian inference, evaluating calibration and robustness
- Run retrospective and live evaluations on active campaign data with clear baselines and metrics
- Present findings to ML and experimental teams, with the option to contribute to a publication
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Pursuing a Master's or PhD in statistics, ML, CS, operations research, applied math, or a quantitative science
- Solid grounding in Bayesian inference and decision making, including priors and posterior predictive distributions
- Research experience in Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, bandits, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modeling
- Strong Python skills with PyTorch and probabilistic libraries such as Pyro, PyMC, or BoTorch
- Comfort working with small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets
- Clear communication with both ML and experimental collaborators
Bonus Points For
- Applying these methods to real problems in materials science, chemistry, or another physical science
- Familiarity with in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference, meta-learning, or prior-data fitted networks
- Optimization over categorical or combinatorial spaces, including mixed-variable, multi-objective, or batch settings
- Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making or Bayesian experimental design
- Training models on multimodal scientific data such as text, images, spectra, or simulations

title: Co-Op, Characterization Electrodeposited Material
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences is hiring a co-op to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. You will characterize electrodeposited metal films and develop the measurement methods that make those results repeatable. Deposition is handled by other scientists on the team; your focus is measurement, method development, and data quality.
The role spans electrical, surface, structural, and mechanical techniques: four-point probe for sheet resistance and resistivity, laser confocal metrology for thickness, step height, and roughness, XRD and EBSD for phase, texture, and grain structure, and hardness testing for mechanical properties. Much of the work is standing these methods up: defining sample prep, acquisition settings, and acceptance criteria so results hold across operators and sample batches.
You will work alongside scientists and engineers in a lab built for high-throughput, automated experimentation, and your protocols will feed directly into how these measurements get scaled.
What You'll Be Building
- Develop sample prep and measurement protocols for general characterization tools on electrodeposited films: four-point probe, hardness testing, and SEM/EBSD.
- Prepare samples for SEM and EBSD (mounting, polishing, surface cleanup)
- Run four-point probe, laser confocal metrology, and hardness measurements
- Analyze XRD data (phase ID, texture, peak shift, crystallite size) and EBSD data (grain size, orientation, texture)
- Validate measurement repeatability and establish data quality criteria
- Analyze and visualize characterization data, then document methods and failure modes
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Mechanical/Chemical Engineering, or a related field
- Hands-on experience operating materials characterization instruments in a lab
- Hands-on experience with hardness testing (micro- or nano-indentation, or others)
- Hands-on experience with metallographic or SEM sample prep
- Experience analyzing XRD data
- Working knowledge of thin films, metal microstructure, or surface metrology
- Careful experimental technique and detailed record keeping
- Available for the full Spring co-op term, January through May

title: Co-Op, IT/OT Security Analyst
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila runs autonomous science facilities — labs full of instruments, robotics, and controllers that produce the experimental data that is the company's core IP. Securing that environment is a different problem from securing laptops and SaaS, and we are building the program from the ground up. This co-op works on that build, not on the side of it.
The role sits at the seam between IT, Lab IT, and OT, spanning four workstreams: OT asset visibility and tooling, vulnerability and patch management across IT/OT, SOC integration and threat intelligence, and program build. The work product outlives the term.
What we are looking for is someone curious enough to trace a problem end to end without being handed the answer, and persistent enough to stay with it when the architecture is not documented anywhere. We will teach the OT domain. We cannot teach that.
What You'll Be Building

title: Co-Op, SCADA Engineer
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila's SCADA system spans cloud and on-premise infrastructure: Ignition gateways on EC2, a historian on RDS PostgreSQL, MQTT brokers, and edge nodes at each site. Today no single view shows the health of all of it, so the team learns about failures from users rather than from monitoring.
As a co-op on the Hardware & Controls Engineering team, you will build that view: a live connectivity diagram showing how every piece connects and which links are up, backed by dashboards covering database, gateway, and edge node health. The work is read-only end to end, with read-only AWS access and SELECT-only database access, so you can explore the full system safely.
You will be based at our Alewife site in Cambridge, working alongside controls engineers and the IT/OT team. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end.
What You'll Be Building
- Build a live topology view of edge nodes, brokers, gateways, and databases with per-link status and last-seen timestamps
- Surface RDS PostgreSQL health: CPU, memory, storage growth, connection counts, replication lag, and slow queries
- Dashboard Ignition gateway and EC2 metrics, including JVM heap, tag quality, Sparkplug birth and death rates, and scan timing
- Monitor on-premise edge nodes for reachability, uptime, resource use, and last publish time
- Integrate existing sources (CloudWatch, Performance Insights, Ignition gateway metrics, broker status) into one interface
- Document the setup so the team can extend and maintain it after the term ends
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field
- Available full time for the Spring 2027 co-op term, on-site at Alewife
- Proficiency in Python for scripting and data collection
- Comfortable working in Linux from the command line
- Working knowledge of networking fundamentals: IP addressing, subnets, ports, and routing
- Clear written communication for documenting dashboards and findings
Bonus Points For
- Exposure to AWS, particularly EC2, RDS, CloudWatch, or IAM
- Experience with Grafana, Prometheus, or similar observability tooling
- Familiarity with Ignition, MQTT or Sparkplug, or other industrial SCADA tooling
- JavaScript or React, useful for building inside Ignition Perspective

You will set the research agenda for models that understand the purpose of a protocol, compose experiments against real laboratory constraints, diagnose failures, and adapt protocols as evidence arrives. title: Engineer II/ Senior Engineer, Robotics Platform Evaluation
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is building a dedicated platform evaluation function within our robotics organization. The team tests and benchmarks alternative robotics platforms, including mobile manipulators, AMRs and AGVs, and other form factors, against our current production baseline. Consistent methodology across platforms is the point: results have to be directly comparable to be useful.
As a Robotics Platform Evaluation Engineer, you own robots end to end. You unbox and commission new hardware, integrate it with our software stack and infrastructure, execute the full test program, and turn the results into decision-ready comparisons that inform which platforms we adopt.
This is a hands-on, systems-level role. You will be in the lab working directly with hardware, not reviewing spec sheets. You will also shape the evaluation methodology and the tooling behind it, so each platform assessment runs faster and more consistently than the last.
What You'll Be Building
- Commission new robotics platforms from unboxing through integration with our stack
- Own end-to-end evaluation of assigned platforms, from test plan to benchmark report
- Run test suites spanning navigation, manipulation, perception, and controls
- Integrate platforms with ROS2 and Nav2, adapting drivers, configurations, and interfaces
- Characterize manipulator, gripper, and AMR/AGV performance against comparable baselines
- Extend the shared evaluation framework and tooling for future platform assessments
- Flag integration issues, safety concerns, and platform limitations early and clearly
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Professional experience deploying robotics platforms in production, commercial, or applied R&D settings
- Hands-on ROS2 and Nav2 experience in real deployments, not simulation alone
- Experience with manipulation and pick-and-place, including motion planning and grasp execution
- Experience with controls for robot arms or mobile bases
- Experience integrating and calibrating camera or lidar perception pipelines
- Direct experience with AMRs/AGVs or 6 to 7 DoF arms, including grippers and end effectors
- Track record turning test results into clear, decision-ready comparisons
Bonus Points For
- Evaluated or compared multiple robotics platforms or vendors head to head
- Experience with mobile manipulators, meaning an arm mounted on a mobile base
- Experience with robotics simulation tools (Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or similar) for platform validation
- Built internal tooling or frameworks for standardized robot testing
- Background in industrial, warehouse, logistics, or manufacturing automation

title: Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator
text:
Your Impact at LILA
The Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator is a hands-on technology role responsible for the day-to-day administration, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of computing infrastructure inside Lila Sciences' laboratory environments. This role owns the layer of technology that sits between corporate IT and operational technology (OT), the workstations, edge compute, lab-area networking, and instrument-adjacent systems that enable autonomous science to run reliably.
Reporting to the Senior Director, OT Security and IT/OT Convergence, the Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator works in close partnership with the OT network architecture team, corporate IT operations, facilities/building automation, and laboratory operations leadership. The successful candidate is comfortable operating in a complex, fast-moving research environment where standard corporate IT practices do not always apply, where change control matters more than speed, and where the end users are scientists running irreplaceable experiments on highly specialized equipment.
This role is a key part of Lila's IT/OT convergence program. In addition to delivering day-to-day operational support, the person hired will contribute to the standards, device catalog, and playbooks that scale the function as the company grows, working under the direction of the Senior Director, OT Security and IT/OT Convergence.
What You'll Be Building
Lab IT Operations and Support
- Provide day-to-day administration and troubleshooting for laboratory computing assets, including lab-area workstations, edge compute nodes, lab-supplied PCs, and dedicated lab-network infrastructure (switches, access points, cabling).
- Respond to and resolve Lab IT incidents and service requests through the enterprise ITSM platform, applying appropriate prioritization for experiments in progress and time-sensitive scientific work.
- Maintain a strong on-site presence across Lila's laboratory locations; observe how scientists and lab operators use technology in practice and proactively identify issues before they become tickets.
- Coordinate scheduled maintenance windows for Lab IT systems in alignment with laboratory operations leadership; ensure changes do not disrupt active experiments.
Instrument-Adjacent and OT Boundary Support
- Provide IT-side support for laboratory instruments and automated platforms, including networking, identity integration, agent deployment decisions, and image/configuration alignment with company standards.
- Partner with the OT network architecture team, instrument vendors, and laboratory automation engineers to support new instrument deployments and changes, recognizing that instrument-connected systems require specialized handling distinct from standard corporate endpoints.
- Troubleshoot authentication, networking, and connectivity issues on vendor-supplied lab equipment, including systems with non-standard configurations, embedded operating systems, or unique vendor account models.
Asset Management and Inventory
- Maintain accurate, current Lab IT asset records in the enterprise CMDB, including device tier, owner, location, configuration baseline, and lifecycle state.
- Apply company labeling standards (QR/barcode asset tags linked to CMDB records) to Lab IT assets and conduct periodic ownership reconciliation.
- Serve as a primary point of contact when security or vulnerability management tools generate alerts on Lab IT assets, executing the workflow of alert review, asset identification, owner notification, and resolution.
Standards, Onboarding, and Procurement Support
- Contribute to the development and ongoing maintenance of the standardized device catalog and golden image program for laboratory computing equipment.
- Support the secure onboarding of new laboratory instruments and platforms, including baseline configuration, segmentation placement, monitoring enrollment, and owner assignment.
- Provide IT/OT review of laboratory procurement requests involving compute or network equipment, ensuring new acquisitions can be supported, secured, and monitored before they are placed into production.
Network and Segmentation Support
- Work alongside the OT network team to support and operate dedicated laboratory network infrastructure, including access points, intermediate distribution switches, and instrument-tier switching.
- Support enterprise network migration and modernization projects from the laboratory side, including SD-WAN cutovers, DHCP and reservation validation, and post-cutover instrument connectivity troubleshooting.
- Identify and remediate drift from segmentation and architecture standards across laboratory sites.
Coordination, Documentation, and Cross-Site Coverage
- Coordinate all lab-impacting technology changes through the established laboratory operations approval channels; uphold change-control discipline as a core principle of the role.
- Translate between the network/architecture, facilities/building-automation, and laboratory operations perspectives; resolve issues that arise at the boundaries between these groups.
- Provide cross-coverage between laboratory sites and partner with managed-service support providers and second-shift resources as the function scales.
- Document Lab IT standards, procedures, and runbooks so the function remains operable, scalable, and onboardable as the team grows.
What You'll Need to Succeed
Required Experience and Education
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field; equivalent professional experience considered.
- 2 to 5 years of hands-on experience in IT systems administration, with a meaningful portion of that experience spent supporting non-standard or specialized environments (laboratories, manufacturing, healthcare clinical environments, broadcast, or similar settings where standard corporate IT practices must be adapted).
- Demonstrated experience supporting users and systems in environments where rebooting, re-imaging, or applying patches on demand is not an acceptable approach, and where coordinated change windows are required.
- Experience working in close partnership with networking, infrastructure, or operational technology teams on shared systems and boundary handoffs.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to scientists, engineers, and executives in language appropriate to each audience.
- Willingness and ability to work on-site at Lila's laboratory locations on a regular basis; this is not a remote role.
Technical Expertise
- Strong Windows administration skills: domain join, group policy, drivers and networking stack, advanced troubleshooting; working comfort with macOS and Linux as they appear on laboratory benches.

title: Machine Learning Scientist, BioML
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is building a platform where AI and automation work together to solve the hardest problems in biomedicine. Within Life Sciences AI (LSAI), we are building the loop where AI, automation and experimental biology co-evolve.
We are seeking a Scientist II/ Senior Scientist, BioML to work at the intersection of mechanistic modeling and experimental design. Helping build the biological mechanism layer of that loop: reasoning systems that take a mechanistic hypothesis apart into what must be true for it to hold, judge what the existing evidence actually settles, and identify what remains open. You will encode what good mechanistic adjudications look like and build the evaluations that measure a system against them.
Then you will help close the loop: at Lila, when the evidence to ground or test a system does not exist, we generate it. You will design experimental campaigns that anchor these systems in real measurement, and own the analysis of the data that comes back. The core of this role is to decide what is worth measuring and closing that loop.
The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on experience in computational biology, BioML, or applied ML for biological data, and can partner effectively with experimental scientists, ML researchers, and platform engineers. This person will help define tractable scientific questions, design rigorous analyses, interpret model outputs in biological context, and contribute to workflows that connect computational predictions with experimental decisions.
This is an individual contributor role for a scientist who wants to drive meaningful applied work in a fast-moving, interdisciplinary environment. The role will emphasize execution, scientific judgment, and cross-functional collaboration rather than group leadership or owning the broader platform direction.
What You'll Be Building
- Encode mechanistic reasoning into systems, and build the evaluations that hold them to it. Turn how a good scientist decomposes a hypothesis — what must be established, in what order, what distinguishes the live alternatives — into structured frameworks and reasoning workflows that operate without you in the loop. Define what a good answer is, and score whether a system reached it for the right reason rather than a plausible-sounding one.
- Analyze the biological data that grounds these systems. Hands-on analysis of single-cell, perturbation, proteomics imaging, and genetic data: build the pipelines that turn raw measurement into model-ready evidence, run the quality control and annotation-stability analyses that determine how much weight a given fact should carry, and produce the quantitative results the reasoning layer depends on.
- Design experimental campaigns and close the loop on them. Specify what to measure, in which contexts, at what precision and scale — both to anchor these systems in real data and to generate outcome-verified cases they can be trained and scored against. Analyze what comes back, update the assessment, and say what changed.
- Build outcome-verifiable benchmarks and set the evidence standards behind them. Including retrodiction sets that score a system on predicting a documented outcome from pre-decision evidence only, with the evidence boundary enforced. Define what counts as direct versus inferred evidence, and when a computational prediction may substitute for a measurement.
- Co-design with ML scientists and engineers, and with experimental scientists. Shape evaluations so they measure decision quality rather than apparent reasoning quality, and ensure outputs carry usable uncertainty.
- Communicate results completely. Publish and present to scientific, engineering, and therapeutic audiences, including the parts of a result that do not support the conclusion people want.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- PhD in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Computational Genomics, Biostatistics, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field , with research centered on biological data.
- Strong hands-on computational and data-analysis depth. Fluent Python; substantial experience analyzing high-dimensional biological data (single-cell omics, perturbation screens, imaging-based proteomics, or genetics) in reproducible, version-controlled pipelines. You will run your own analyses and evaluations and interpret them yourself.
- Mechanistic biology fluency. Able to reason about a pathway or drug mechanism step by step: what is rate-limiting, what would be observed if it were, what evidence distinguishes the alternatives, and what a given assay can and cannot establish. This is what you will be encoding.
- Evidence judgment, and the instinct to make it into a system. Demonstrated ability to assess whether data support a claim and to reason about what was knowable when — combined with an interest in making that judgment reproducible by something other than you, through structure, schemas, or evaluation.
- Clear communication. Ability to explain methods, assumptions, results, and limitations to both technical and interdisciplinary audiences.
Bonus Points For
- Deep analysis experience in at least one of: perturbation screens, single-cell omics, imaging-based proteomics, or functional genomics.
- Depth in immune cell biology, cell therapy, or targeted delivery — receptor engagement, trafficking, or effector function.
- Experience with lab-in-the-loop or closed-loop workflows, active learning, or experiment selection.
- Experience evaluating language models or agents on scientific judgment tasks, including contamination and memorization controls.
- Experience designing or applying structured evidence frameworks, curated resources, or controlled vocabularies that other people depend on.

text:

We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. As scientific AI systems become more capable and autonomous, their safety assessment and safeguards must develop alongside them. title: Scientist I/II, Characterization and Composition Analysis
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences is seeking a Scientist I/II, Characterization and Composition Analysis to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. The Autonomous Science Platform combines experimental science, automation, AI, and software to accelerate materials discovery. This role turns elemental measurements into trusted, machine-readable composition data that supports scientific decisions, automated workflows, and model development.
This is a hybrid experimental and software-facing role, centered on hands-on characterization with substantial analyzer development. You will work with X-ray fluorescence (XRF), SEM-based energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), wavelength-dispersive spectroscopy (WDS), and related analytical instruments. title: Scientist II/Senior Scientist, Solid-State Materials
text:
Your Impact at LILA
As a Scientist II/Senior Scientist on the Vacuum Synthesis team at Lila Sciences, you will advance the design and synthesis of functional inorganic solid-state materials in support of Lila's autonomous science platform. You will design and execute multi-step preparations across diverse chemical systems, turning phase-diagram and crystal-chemistry reasoning into prioritized synthesis pathways and experimental feedback. You will partner with other synthetic materials scientists, characterization scientists, ML researchers, and systems engineers to close the synthesis-characterization-modeling loop and accelerate Lila's path to scientific superintelligence in functional materials.
What You'll Be Building
- Design and execute synthesis campaigns across multiple chemical systems and structure families, drawing on the breadth of solid-state preparative chemistry (melt routes, flux, vapor transport, soft-chemical, topochemical, single-crystal growth, and unconventional or high-pressure environments as the target phase demands).
- Translate phase-diagram, crystal-chemistry, and structure-property reasoning into concrete, prioritized synthesis pathways for novel functional inorganic compounds.
- Access metastable and kinetically trapped phases through appropriate low-temperature and soft-chemical routes.
- Work with the characterization team to develop routine and specialized structural characterization workflows (powder XRD, phase ID, refinement) for materials identification and quality control.
- Take synthesized materials through to functional property screening (magnetic, transport, optical, or related) in partnership with the characterization team and use the resulting data to refine target selection and synthesis design.
- Partner with materials simulation scientists, ML researchers, and systems engineers to integrate synthesis outputs into closed-loop, AI-guided experimental workflows.

What You'll Need to Succeed
- PhD in Solid-State Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related field, with 1–5 years of postdoctoral or industry experience.

- Demonstrated experience performing materials synthesis campaigns driven by functional property targets (e.g., magnetism, nonlinear optical response, exotic charge transport, or related phenomena).

title: Senior Director, Software Development, Test Automation
text:
Your Impact at LILA
The Role
We're hiring a Senior Director, Software Development, Test Automation Systems to architect and build Lila's test automation platform and quality engineering practice for our AI-powered scientific and lab automation products. Reporting to the VP of Engineering, you'll own the test automation system, CI/CD test infrastructure, AI-driven test tooling, and the eval discipline that hold the bar across our SDLC.
This is a builder-leader role. You will drive the quality vision, write requirements, make sharp build-vs-buy calls, drive execution, and build and lead a small (3–5 person) team that delivers leverage. The operating model is federated: you own the platform, standards, and metrics; engineering teams own test execution. You scale through tooling and influence.
As you scale into this role, you'll also stand up the QC framework for our lab automation system — the validation patterns, harnesses, and contracts that science operations teams will operate day-to-day. Data integrity and ALCOA+ compliance are foundational to everything you build.
What You'll Be Building
What You'll Do
Architect and ship the test automation platform
- Design and build the test automation platform — frameworks, fixtures, golden datasets, test orchestration, and reporting — that the engineering org adopts by default
- Set standards across unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, regression, performance, and chaos testing for backend services, the frontend monorepo, and data pipelines
- Treat platform adoption, flake rate, and time-to-signal as first-class engineering metrics
Make build-vs-buy decisions with conviction
- Own the buy/build/borrow strategy across test infrastructure, eval platforms, browser/device clouds, observability, and lab QC tooling
- Justify every choice with TCO, signal quality, integration cost, and time-to-leverage — and revisit decisions as the org and tech landscape evolve
- Bias toward leverage: buy commodity capabilities, build the differentiators (Lila-specific AI evals, lab QC, scientific data integrity)
Modernize CI/CD for fast, reliable signal
- Own the test execution layer of CI/CD: parallelization, caching, hermetic environments, ephemeral preview envs, and affected-only test selection across our Nx monorepo/microservices.
- Build retry, quarantine, and impact-analysis systems so signal stays sharp as the org scales
- Drive change-failure rate, MTTR, Test effectiveness, pipeline efficiency, coverage, and PR-to-prod lead time as outcomes
Drive AI-driven test automation
- Apply LLMs across the full test lifecycle: test generation from specs and PRs, self-healing UI tests, synthesis, visual regression with vision models, and AI-assisted failure triage
- Validate every AI-generated test through evals — no LLM-authored test ships without proof it doesn't degrade signal
- Establish the eval discipline for Lila's AI/agent stack: golden datasets, rubrics, regression suites, offline + online evaluation pipelines
Define and operate the quality metrics system
- Define quality SLOs and adoption metrics by team and service: coverage, escape rate, MTTR, change-failure rate, eval pass rate, lab QC violation rate
- Build dashboards that make quality visible from PR to executive review
- Apply Google SRE practices to prioritize where investment goes
Mid-long term - Stand up the QC framework for lab automation
- Design the validation framework, harnesses, and contracts that lab and Science Ops teams will operate
- Embed ALCOA+ principles: data integrity, audit trails, lineage from sample → instrument → output
- Partner with Research Ops on pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight validation patterns for autonomous lab execution
Lead and coach across the engineering org
- Build a 3–5 person team of test automation engineers focused on platform leverage, not on writing tests for other teams
- Coach engineering teams on test design, quality investments, and adoption — make it cheaper to test well than to ship blind
- Translate UX and customer issues into testable contracts and platform improvements
First 6–12 Month Outcomes
- First 90 days: Establish baselines — flake rate, time-to-signal, change-failure rate, coverage, and current build-vs-buy footprint — and publish a quality scorecard with the first set of SLOs. Hire or onboard the initial 1–2 platform engineers.
- By 6 months: Ship v1 of the test automation platform adopted by at least one flagship engineering team by default; land CI/CD test-execution improvements (parallelization, affected-only selection, flake quarantine) with measurable time-to-signal reduction. Stand up the eval discipline (golden datasets, rubrics, regression suites) for the AI/agent stack.
- By 12 months: Drive default platform adoption across the engineering org; demonstrate AI-driven test automation in production with eval-gated rollout. Deliver the first operating version of the lab automation QC framework with ALCOA+ audit trails, validated end-to-end with Science Ops. Quality is visible from PR to executive review via live dashboards.
What You'll Need to Succeed
Required Qualifications
- 10+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years leading test automation, quality engineering, or platform/SRE-adjacent functions
- 3+ years managing engineers, including building or scaling a team
- Strong software architect/engineer. You write designs your team wants to read and review. Python and/or Typescript hands on expertise is highly desirable.
- Deep CI/CD expertise. GitHub Actions or equivalent at scale, monorepo build/test orchestration (Nx, Turborepo, or Bazel), test parallelization and caching, hermetic environments, ephemeral preview envs, flake quarantine, and test impact analysis
- Demonstrated build-vs-buy judgment. You've made and defended decisions on test infra, eval platforms, browser/device clouds, and observability — and can articulate the TCO and signal trade-offs that drove them
- Hands-on AI-driven test automation experience. Using LLMs to generate, maintain, or triage tests in production, with rigorous eval validation. Fluency with eval frameworks
- Track record of standing up a test automation platform that engineering teams adopted — not one bolted on
- Working knowledge of Google's SRE practices and a point of view on when they apply to pre-production quality
- Metrics-driven leader who drives outcomes through platform leverage and influence, not gatekeeping
- Customer- and UX-first instincts: treats test automation as a vehicle for user experience, not a cost center
Bonus Points For
Nice to Have
- Experience in GxP-regulated environments or scientific data integrity programs
- Experience with lab automation, LIMS, or other instrument-driven systems
- Multi-tenant SaaS quality at scale
- Exposure to event-driven systems, agent orchestration frameworks, or MCP
- Performance/load testing or chaos engineering background

title: Senior Manager, Scientific Discovery Capacity Planning

You will own the models, processes, and cross-functional rhythms that translate demand from go-to-market commitments partnerships into the delivery and operational capacity required to meet it profitably. Capacity planning is the connective tissue between what we sell and what we can deliver. Done well, it lets Lila commit confidently to customers and partners, invest ahead of demand without waste, and grow the commercial business on a sound operational footing. You'll be the person who makes that discipline real.
This is a highly cross-functional role positioned at the intersection of Finance, Product, Commercial, AI, and Experimental teams. The successful candidate will serve as the primary point of contact for capacity and resourcing across the proposal pipeline, establish the source of truth for capacity commitments, and design the system required to scale our AI Science Factories.
What You'll Be Building
- Build, own, and execute end-to-end capacity planning processes for every commercial proposal and scientific capability.
- Translate demand forecasts into resource, staffing, and capacity plans while identifying bottlenecks and quantifying the cost and lead time to close them.
- Maintain the authoritative record of capacity commitments across the active pipeline.

title: Senior ML Scientist, Biological Systems
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is redefining the future of medicine by combining automated large-scale data generation with scientific superintelligence. At Lila, we are building the loop where AI, automation, and experimental biology co-evolve to solve the hardest problems in medicine.
The Life Science AI team develops machine learning systems for automated reasoning on biological data, combining state-of-the-art ML with breakthrough biology. We seek a Senior ML Scientist to focus on domain models underneath that system: models of perturbation biology, genetics, and and high-dimensional experimental readouts that connect biological mechanism, experimental intervention and therapeutic opportunity.
At Lila, the data is generated for the model: we run our own experiments at scale, and you will help decide what gets measured. The question is not only what to learn from a fixed dataset, but what datasets should exist. And model outputs are reasoned over. Predictions go to systems and scientists choosing what to run next and making mechanistic calls downstream. Both need to know why, not only what. A model that returns a quantity a biologist, human or AI, can argue with; models that transfer to new contexts, compose into a downstream calculation, and can be checked against an independent measurement are often worth more than a more accurate one that returns an embedding.
What You'll Be Building
- Build domain models for perturbation, genetic, and multimodal experimental data, and translate biological questions into rigorous ML problem formulations. Where the biology supports it, build models with interpretable structure — representations grounded in the machinery that executes a biological process rather than in cell-type identity embeddings, and parameters a biologist can argue with.
- Make uncertainty a deliverable. Calibrated posteriors, honest error bars, and outputs that tell a downstream consumer how much a prediction can actually settle — particularly when predicting into conditions never measured.
- Pre-register and beat baselines. Simple entity-mean, additive, and linear baselines are stated before any model is fit. If the full model does not beat them, we ship the baseline and say so.
- Partner with experimental scientists to guide data generation and model validation — shaping what gets measured, in what contexts, at what precision — and build the experiment-selection methods that choose the next batch of measurements to reduce uncertainty where it matters.
- Design benchmarks that connect model performance to biological and therapeutic consequence, apply model outputs to prioritize targets and mechanisms, and contribute technical direction to high-impact modeling programs.
- Support the integration of domain models into agentic workflows. Deploy tools, help engineer the agent harnesses that incorporate these tools and collaborate on creating environments to train the reasoning models that drive these agents.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- PhD in machine learning, statistics, computational biology, computer science, bioengineering, physics, or a related quantitative field, with a strong publication record or equivalent industry impact.
- Experience developing models for high-dimensional biological data, and the judgment to connect ML methods to biological mechanism and experimental design.
- Generalization under structured sparsity. A track record of building models that predict into conditions not directly observed — sparse or unbalanced experimental designs, held-out combinations, transfer to new contexts — rather than interpolating within a densely sampled corpus.
- Uncertainty and evaluation rigor. Comfort with calibration, proper scoring rules, and evaluation design, in work where someone made a decision based on your numbers.
- Strong programming skills, reliable ML research workflows, and clear communication across ML, biology, and experimental teams. Track record of leading ambiguous research problems from formulation through execution.
- Communicate findings clearly to technical and cross-functional audiences, including scientists, engineers, product partners, and therapeutic stakeholders.
- Support external scientific visibility through publications, presentations, and engagement with ML/AI for Biology, computational biology and therapeutic discovery communities, as appropriate.
Bonus Points For
- Mechanistic and probabilistic modeling — the strongest differentiator for this role. Bayesian hierarchical models, simulation-based or likelihood-free inference, amortized posterior inference, state-space or ODE-based models, neural differential equations, or mechanism-informed ML. Also relevant from outside biology: pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic, systems-biology, or physical modeling where the parameters had to mean something.
- Experience with models in at least one of these areas:
- Familiarity with active learning, Bayesian optimal experimental design, closed-loop experimentation, or lab-in-the-loop systems.
- Experience deploying research models into scientific decision-making workflows, including serving models as tools other systems call.

title: Staff/Principal Engineer, Search & Retrieval
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences is building the infrastructure for autonomous science: AI systems that design experiments, run them in physical labs, and close the loop across life sciences, chemistry, and materials science. Our platform enables this to operate reliably at scale for external customers who require security, auditability, and operational rigor.
We're hiring a Staff/Principal Engineer, Search & Retrieval (Enterprise AI) to own how scientists and agents ask questions of scientific knowledge at Lila: published literature and patents, customer-supplied documents, lab protocols, and the structured experimental record.
Your work will involve building RAG over unstructured text and a scientific knowledge graph that links literature to the structured experimental record.
Enterprise customers require one retrieval platform that any scientific workload can build on, with tenancy enforced in the index and the graph rather than the application layer. You will own that stack end to end, from ingestion to retrieval to cited answers a scientist can trace back to the evidence.
This is a deeply technical senior individual contributor role. We move fast, ship often, and look for engineers who do well with ambiguity and enjoy shaping the problem as much as solving it.
What You'll Be Building
- Technical leadership across platform engineering, infrastructure, AI/ML, and scientific teams. Broad architectural influence, high autonomy, direct ownership of critical platform systems.
- Define the shared retrieval foundation. Your architecture decisions become the default for scientific workloads across the company, well beyond the first one you ship.
- Knowledge graph and graph retrieval. Build one scientific knowledge graph from literature and the structured experimental record. Own graph retrieval and its fusion with vector and lexical search into a single cited answer.
- Agentic search. Build the autonomous research loop, from query planning through retrieval to traceable reasoning.
- Retrieval quality. Own the retrieval pipeline end to end and the evaluation harness.
- Ingestion and extraction. Own the pipeline that turns the many types of scientific data (PDFs, patents, lab protocols, and more) into semantically searchable evidence.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- 8+ years of software development experience, including production ownership of a search, retrieval, RAG, or knowledge graph system that real users depended on.
- Production experience building semantic search: embedding models, vector indexes (HNSW/IVF), hybrid lexical and vector retrieval, and reranking. Graph database experience is a strong plus.
- Track record in high-growth environments where speed-to-value mattered as much as long-term architecture.
- You can describe how you measured retrieval quality (recall, groundedness, citation accuracy) and how you caught regressions.
- Hands-on coding in Python and modern backend frameworks (FastAPI, async Python).
- Modern cloud-native architectures (Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS).
- Strong cross-functional communication and the ability to influence architecture across teams.
- BS, MS, or Ph.D. in Computer Science or a related field of study, or equivalent experience.
Bonus Points For
- Shipped RAG or semantic search in a regulated or enterprise context, through security and compliance review under regimes such as SOC 2, HIPAA, GxP (including ALCOA+ data integrity), or FedRAMP.
- Permission-aware retrieval over access-controlled data.
- Document understanding at scale: OCR, layout-aware parsing, table and figure extraction from scientific literature.
- Agentic retrieval and GraphRAG patterns, and how to evaluate them.
- Platforms serving scientific or laboratory data such as LIMS, ELN, bioinformatics, or materials informatics, with an understanding of provenance and traceability requirements.
- Domain-specific corpora and scientific ontologies (UMLS, MeSH, ChEBI, GO, UniProt, Materials Project) where specialized vocabulary limits general-purpose embeddings and entity linking.
- Knowledge graph construction and graph retrieval: property graph or RDF stores.

title: Staff / Principal Security Engineer, AI Safety and Security
location: Cambridge, MA USA; London, UK; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is developing AI systems for scientific discovery, connecting advanced models with scientific tools and automated laboratories. As these systems become more capable, we need to understand how they could be misused or compromised, which protections matter most, and how to establish that those protections work together.
We're hiring an experienced security practitioner to lead this work at the boundary between AI safety and security. You will investigate real systems, develop threat models, test important assumptions and recommend the protections needed for particular capabilities and deployments. Your work will address both dangerous misuse and the protection of sensitive models, data and research.
This is an opportunity to help shape a developing area of AI safety through security practice. You will combine technical investigation with careful analysis and clear writing, working closely with our established Security team, researchers and engineers to turn findings into implemented improvements.
You will bring security depth and develop your understanding of model capabilities, evaluations and safeguards through that work. Prior experience in AI safety is welcome, but not required.
What You'll Be Building
- Threat-model consequential systems and capabilities. Investigate how dangerous misuse or compromise could occur across models, deployed services and scientific workflows. Identify the relevant actors, access routes and failure paths, and the protections that could interrupt them.
- Test the assumptions behind our defenses. Examine architectures, code, configurations and operational evidence. Run focused adversarial tests, build prototypes and investigate weaknesses, including situations where several protections depend on the same underlying system.
- Shape the protections needed for safe deployment. Turn dangerous-capability assessments into concrete security requirements. Assess how compromise of models, sensitive assets or supporting systems changes the safety assessment, drawing on personnel, physical and other security specialists where relevant.
- Make evidence-based recommendations. Define what evidence would demonstrate that important controls and safeguards work together. Combine findings from model evaluations and security testing, explain the remaining uncertainty, and recommend improvements or conditions for use.
- Carry findings through to practical improvements. Work with Security, Safety and engineering owners to prioritize changes, specify acceptance criteria and verify the results. Make clear recommendations about which gaps require attention first and why.
- Anticipate what more capable systems will require. Identify where changes in capability, access or deployment call for stronger protections. Help teams plan security work with long lead times, and update assessments as systems change or new evidence emerges.
- Develop methods that others can use. Turn your investigations into clear threat models, assessment methods and technical guidance. Help Safety and Security colleagues apply the approach to new problems and build a shared understanding of the evidence behind decisions.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Substantial hands-on security experience and deep expertise in at least one relevant discipline , such as security architecture, application or infrastructure security, offensive security, or incident response. You can reason across disciplines and identify when specialist judgment is needed.
- A record of resolving consequential security problems. You have investigated ambiguous risks, challenged designs and followed improvements through to validation, including work involving several teams.
- Strong technical judgment. You can examine unfamiliar systems, scrutinize code and configurations where relevant, and use technical investigation or testing to distinguish plausible claims from demonstrated protection.
- Curiosity about AI safety and scientific systems. You want to understand how model capabilities and safeguards are evaluated, can learn unfamiliar domains quickly, and reason carefully when evidence is incomplete.
- Clear writing and effective collaboration. You can explain a technical argument precisely, work through disagreements with specialists and turn a complex investigation into an actionable recommendation.
Bonus Points For
- Securing ML infrastructure, model assets, research environments or AI agents.
- Evaluating safeguards, adversarial robustness or defenses against sophisticated threats.
- Translating risk assessments into technical requirements, assurance evidence or deployment decisions.
- Working in scientific or other environments where digital access can have significant real-world consequences.
We value demonstrated security depth, sound judgment and the ability to learn. A research PhD or experience in every security discipline is not required.
Your early work will help establish how Lila combines safety and security evidence to make concrete decisions about its systems.

We are seeking a Staff or Principal Software Engineer, Scientific System of Record  to join our Scientific System of Record Team and help define and build the next-generation AI-driven scientific platform.
In this role, you will serve as a technical leader for systems that connect scientific intent, laboratory execution, data capture, and AI-driven analysis. You’ll work closely with ML researchers, platform engineers, data engineers, product teams, and scientists to turn complex scientific processes into scalable, elegant software systems. These systems will need to support diverse workloads across structured SQL databases, data lakehouses, workflow engines, and lab execution environments.
This is an opportunity to set technical direction for a cutting-edge AI platform with real scientific impact. If you are passionate about building high-leverage systems, mentoring strong engineers, and solving ambiguous problems at the intersection of AI, software, and science, we would love to hear from you.
About The Team
The Scientific System of Record Team (SSR) builds the memory layer for Lila's operations. It answers two questions: what did we plan to build? and what actually happened? These systems connect scientific intent to physical reality. Together with the data and automation teams, their systems ensure reproducibility and close the Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) loop.

- Databases: Strong experience with SQL and at least one of NoSQL, vector databases, graph databases, search systems, or data lakehouse architectures.

- Orchestration Systems: Experience with orchestrators tools (Airflow, Prefect, Temporal, Dagster).
- Familiarity with Python for Science : Familiarity with data science and ML libraries (pandas, numpy, scipy, jax, pytorch).

title: Supply Chain Demand Planner
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is building a supply chain function, and this is the first hire into it. You will shape the discipline rather than inherit it, owning what happens to an order after it is placed: confirmation, delivery, install and commissioning.
With many active suppliers and a wide set of research and operating groups, deciding which categories earn a demand plan first, and being able to validate that choice, is a central part of the work.
You will work alongside the Procurement team, Category Managers and the Procurement Specialist, so that the supplier relationship, the order and the delivery picture become one end-to-end view rather than three separate ones.
What You'll Be Building
- Build an order tracking system from placement through install and commissioning, designed to migrate into a future ERP.
- Lead and coordinate the supply chain ERP proposal process.
- Own the long-lead item list and make lead times the business can plan around.
- Work down aging open orders and give Finance a clean view of supply commitments.
- Prioritize which categories earn a demand plan and build consumption-based demand signals.
- Size blanket orders to planned build activity and stand up a parts-on-hand model with FP&A.
- Run the delivery and capacity cadence with strategic partners, escalating when dates move.
- Partner with Procurement, Facilities, Lab Operations and Hardware & Controls on receiving and install readiness.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Three to six years in supply chain, demand or materials planning, or order management.
- Track record of owning delivery dates end to end.
- Judgement to prioritize what gets planned, and to defend that order.
- Strong spreadsheet and data skills, translating transactional data into a supply chain view.
- Experience coordinating across suppliers, freight and internal receiving.
- Comfortable with shifting priorities in an early-stage function.
- Comfort building from nothing, starting simple rather than perfect.
Bonus Points For
- Smartsheet or comparable workflow tools.
- Capital equipment installation and commissioning coordination.
- Scientific instruments, lab consumables or another regulated environment.
- ERP planning module implementation such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle or Dynamics.
- Exposure to import, customs or export control.
Compensation
We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

title: Technical Program Manager, AI Data
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
Lila is building toward scientific superintelligence, which depends on a steady supply of high-quality, purpose-built AI data. We're looking for a Senior or Principal Technical Program Manager to join our AI Research team to drive multiple AI data generation and curation workstreams — standing up new project teams, keeping them on schedule, and incorporating that data into the model training pipeline.
You don't need to be an ML researcher, but you must be genuinely curious about how AI data fuels model development and able to clearly articulate what your programs will deliver. The successful candidate thrives in ambiguity, communicates exceptionally well across audiences, and knows how to build clarity and momentum on a fast-paced, rapidly scaling team.
What You'll Be Building
- Launch and operate cross-functional project teams that produce AI data for scientific superintelligence, ensuring each team executes with at high velocity and delivers standardized outputs the model training team can directly consume.
- Serve as the key communication interface between project teams and the research, science, and model training organizations; set up the organizational information flows that allow this communication to happen with speed at scale.
- Drive accountability across distributed, cross-functional teams without relying on direct authority; build consensus through clear communication and sound judgment.
- Define and enforce data delivery standards, QA gates, and handoff protocols so model training receives consistent, high-quality inputs across all active project teams.
- Implement best practices for rapid experimentation and iteration, enabling new project teams to ramp efficiently as additional data initiatives come online.
- Develop clear documentation and reporting to communicate vision, track progress, and align project team work with broader AI Research priorities; represent program status and risks accurately even when the picture is uncertain or evolving.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.
- 8+ years of program or project management experience in the technology or life sciences field.
- Proven experience leading cross-functional programs and driving them to successful completion under tight delivery timelines.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn technical and data requirements into actionable program roadmaps.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; track record of producing executive-quality documents, roadmaps, and updates that drive decisions.
Bonus Points For
- Direct experience in AI/ML research or product organizations, ideally in a program management or research operations capacity.
- Working familiarity with model training data pipelines, dataset curation, or ML evaluation workflows — sufficient to engage credibly with researchers and ask good questions.
- Experience managing programs that produce standardized outputs for downstream technical consumers (e.g., model training, eval, or platform teams).
- Enthusiastic about emerging technologies and experienced in driving rapid experimentation and program iteration.

title: Technical Recruiter, AI Research
location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
text:
Your Impact at LILA
As an AI Research Recruiter at Lila Sciences, you will partner directly with our AI research and engineering teams to identify, engage, and hire the researchers and engineers building our AI-driven platform. This is a strategic, full-cycle role: you'll shape hiring plans with research leadership, build Lila's reputation in the AI research community, and go deep in high-signal technical channels to reach talent that isn't sitting on a job board.
What You'll Be Building
- Develop and execute strategic recruiting plans for AI/ML research and engineering roles, from hiring-manager intake through screen, interview loop management, offer strategy, and close.
- Partner with AI Research hiring managers and interview panels to translate team needs into sourcing strategy, candidate personas, and role calibration.
- Build and sustain a high-trust network of ML researchers and applied scientists across subfields (LLM, RL, Generative AI) through consistent relationship-building, community presence, and non-traditional discovery loops (research publications, GitHub, conferences, open-source).
- Partner with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to map long-term AI/ML talent strategy and balance hiring priorities across research teams.
- Build and iterate on recruiting processes that maintain a high, consistent talent bar while actively removing bias from the hiring process.
- Strengthen Lila's employer brand within the ML research and scientific community — representing our mission, culture, and technical work to candidates with strong options elsewhere.
- Stay current on sourcing techniques, interview innovation, and AI/ML talent-market trends; bring new approaches back to the team.
- Maintain operational rigor: pipeline hygiene, recruiting metrics (time-to-fill, slate quality, source efficacy), and clear communication with candidates and hiring teams.
What You'll Need to Succeed
- 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience supporting technical research teams, with a track record of recruiting AI/ML research talent specifically.
- Strong existing network in the ML research community (NeurIPS, ICML, top CS/ML programs).
- Proven ability to attract passive candidates from leading academic institutions and frontier labs, and to scale a high-performing technical hiring function.
- Strong technical aptitude — comfortable understanding and evaluating ML/research qualifications alongside hiring teams.
- Excellent negotiation, communication, and stakeholder-management skills with senior technical leaders.
- Comfortable operating with autonomy and juggling shifting priorities in a fast-moving environment.
Bonus Points For
- Hands-on experience with agentic recruiting tools/workflows (automations, enrichment/triage helpers) to improve candidate discovery.
- Experience recruiting at a deep-tech or frontier AI research organization.
- International recruiting experience across multiple regions.
